text:
ashley: Hey team, heads up — since ~03:14 UTC we're seeing a cluster-wide spike of GPU pod evictions in us-west-2. Kubelet network health checks are flapping and marking nodes NotReady briefly which triggers evictions for our long-running training pods. Not sure if it's MTU, RDMA, or the netprobe daemon.

raj: I'm seeing the same. Eviction reason on pods is 'NodeNotReady' / 'NetworkUnavailable'. A bunch of affected nodes have Mellanox NICs and jumbo MTU enabled.

mina: netprobe agent logs from one affected node: 
```
2026-02-28T03:15:21Z netprobe[2123]: probe to 10.32.0.1 failed: 100% packet loss
2026-02-28T03:15:22Z netprobe[2123]: marking interface cni0 as unhealthy
```
But when I ssh onto host and run `ping -I cni0 10.32.0.1 -c 5` it works with 0% loss. Suspicious.

linus: Could be MTU mismatch between host NIC (9000) and CNI bridge (1500) causing fragmentation that netprobe handles poorly. Also saw kernel messages on mlx5 after a recent driver update. Posting quick `ip link` and `kubectl describe node` snippets: 
```
# ip link show | grep -E "eth|cni"
2: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
45: cni0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc noqueue state UP mode DEFAULT group default

# kubectl describe node ip-10-0-1-23
Conditions:
  Type             Status    LastHeartbeatTime
  ----             ------    -----------------
  NetworkUnavailable  True    2026-02-28T03:15:22Z
```

ashley: ops-bot flagged ~30 evictions in a 5m window, many on dedicated-gpu-pool (reserved capacity). This is hurting costs — jobs restart and we end up double-running. :grimacing:

ops-bot: @channel automatic alert: 30 evictions detected on pool dedicated-gpu-pool in us-west-2 between 03:14-03:19 UTC. Incident created: INC-20260228-37.

sre-oncall: Quick triage notes: netprobe false positives -> candidates: MTU mismatch, CNI plugin misconfig (calico/flannel mtu config), recent kernel/driver bump touching mlx5, or transient routing flaps in the VPC.

raj: Quick mitigation plan I executed on 3 nodes: cordon -> drain (with --ignore-daemonsets) -> set `sysctl net.ipv4.route.flush=1` -> restarted calico-node and netprobe daemon -> uncordon. Evictions stopped on those nodes. We'll need a global fix.

mina: Proposed config change: update netprobe to use larger packet size and increase timeout and retries, and to use host-side nsenter network test instead of containerized probe. That should reduce false negatives while we investigate MTU/driver.

linus: Long term we should standardize MTU across host <-> CNI and validate on node boot. For RDMA nodes, add a preflight that ensures `ip link set dev cni0 mtu 9000` or set calico `mtu: 9000` for that pool. Also rolling back the recent mlx5 driver on a canary node showed stable behavior.

ashley: Agreed. Action items: 1) eng-infra to push netprobe config tweak (mina) 2) eng-infra to rollout MTU normalization script for GPU pool (linus) 3) ops to review recent driver rollout and pin driver on dedicated-gpu-pool (raj) 4) cost/sre to calculate cost impact of evictions (ashley). I'll open a tracking ticket and link INC-20260228-37. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: Adding note: for immediate safety we should add a kubelet fallback so short NetworkUnavailable toggles don't trigger hard eviction for pods with critical tolerations for GPUs. I'll PR a small kubelet flag change we can flip cluster-wide if needed.

ashley: Thanks. Will post status updates here. If anyone sees more evictions, ping @sre-oncall and add node hostname.

(reacts: :eyes: :hammer: on several posts)
